messages:
Olivia Grant: Flagging a quality regression we’re seeing under FP8 on long-context for `llama-3.1-70b-instruct` (32k). Not seeing it on 8k/4k cases. Symptoms: more repetition + occasional format drift on structured-output prompts.

Olivia Grant: This popped in the `quantization_quality_sanity_suite` run from last night + a couple of our long-context RAG prompts in suite v3.

Olivia Grant: Numbers (quick + dirty): long-context slice (prompt_len p95 ~ 24k, gen_len ~ 512)
- Baseline BF16: pass rate 96.8%
- FP8: pass rate 92.1% (mostly JSON schema violations + "looping")
- INT8: pass rate 95.9%

Olivia Grant: Attaching the failing cases list + diffs (internal): https://drive.google.com/…/quality-vs-quantization-evals-summary (tab "LC_fp8_regress_llama70b")

Arjun Desai: :eyes: thanks. Is this with the new FP8 attention kernel enabled or just FP8 GEMMs?

Olivia Grant: This was with `--kernel_mode=fp8` end-to-end (so attention + matmul on the FP8 path). I can rerun with attention forced to baseline.

Priyanka Bose: I saw something similar in my repro runs when context >16k. The regression correlates w/ higher KV cache pressure and a couple cases where we hit our "fast-path" scaling config.

Priyanka Bose: Do we have the exact config flags captured for those runs (amax calibration source, per-tensor vs per-channel)?

Rina Kobayashi: Harness is exporting metadata now (post pr-19880) but last night’s job was on the older runner :/ I can re-run with metadata capture + pinned clocks.

Claire Dubois: Before we decide gating, can we rule out runner variance / nondeterminism? This looks like quality not perf, but we’ve had weirdness when driver mismatches happen.

Rina Kobayashi: Driver was 550.54 on that cluster, CUDA 12.4 container. I can re-run on the pinned image from benchmark-lab pr-851 to be safe.

Jonas Weber: We should treat this as "default enable" blocker for FP8 on that model until we understand. Proposed next step:
1) confirm repro w/ pinned runner
2) isolate whether it’s attention FP8 or matmul FP8
3) if still present, add gating rule for long-context (e.g., disable FP8 above N tokens) + require eval signoff for changing that threshold.

Grace Kim: +1. We’ve seen attention FP8 be touchy on long seq for a few shapes. If it’s attention-only, we can keep FP8 GEMMs + baseline attention (perf hit but safer).

Grace Kim: Do you have any signal whether failures cluster on specific head_dim / hidden_size? (llama70b is 8192 hidden, head_dim 128 iirc)

Olivia Grant: Not that granular yet. Failures cluster on prompts with big retrieved context + structured output. It’s not all long-context, but it’s more frequent as prompt_len increases.

Yuki Sato: For rollout: we can implement a dispatch guard in the kernel auto-select:
- FP8 allowed only if prompt_len <= 16k for `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- or "FP8 attention disabled" when prompt_len > 16k (keep FP8 matmul)
We already have shape-regime rules in the heuristics; adding a per-model override is straightforward.

Noah Patel: Please make sure any gating is reflected in perf canary dimensions too. Otherwise canary will compare apples/oranges when traffic mix shifts.

Jonas Weber: +1 and we should document explicitly in the quant profile policy ("FP8 long-context exceptions").

Arjun Desai: If INT8 is basically baseline quality here, we could flip long-context to INT8 as the "quantized default" for this model (assuming perf is still decent). But would like to see perf impact.

Grace Kim: INT8 attention is not in scope right now; INT8 gains mostly from GEMMs. If we keep attention baseline either way, INT8 vs FP8 might be closer.

Olivia Grant: Action items from my side:
- rerun 3-way ablation on the long-context subset:
  a) BF16 baseline
  b) FP8 matmul only (attention baseline)
  c) FP8 attention + FP8 matmul
  d) INT8 matmul only (attention baseline)
and share pass rates + 20 example failures.

Priyanka Bose: I’ll also try an alternate calibration profile for FP8 (per-channel activation scaling) on llama70b LC slice. Might reduce the drift.

Claire Dubois: For methodology: can we define LC slice precisely (prompt_len distribution, doc count, retrieval ordering)? so we can cite it later and not fight "it depends".

Olivia Grant: Yep. Using suite v3 `rag_long_context_v2` prompts (doc_count 8-12, shuffled) + gen_len capped 512. I’ll paste the exact suite selector once the rerun is kicked off.

Rina Kobayashi: I can queue the rerun today on the pinned runner. ETA 3-4 hours for the full ablation. Will include metadata: git SHA, driver/CUDA, clocks, model hash, quant profile ID.

Jonas Weber: In parallel, I’m leaning to add a conservative guardrail now (so we don’t accidentally default-enable FP8 LC).
Proposal: "FP8 attention disabled for llama70b when prompt_len > 12k" until we have a clean story.

Yuki Sato: If we want a fast safety patch, I can add a server-side override in the kernel registry config (no code release needed) but it needs a clear condition (prompt_len threshold) + model id.

Noah Patel: If it’s server-side config, still route it through the perf canary gate config so we can observe error rate / format violations after the change.

Arjun Desai: +1. Also add note: any change in default quant profile should require Applied ML signoff (Jonas) + at least the LC slice passing.

Grace Kim: If the ablation shows attention FP8 is the culprit, we can keep FP8 matmul path wide open. That’s still a meaningful cost win and avoids the "attention FP8" risk.

Olivia Grant: Sounds good. I’ll post results back here once the reruns finish.

Rina Kobayashi: Kicked off job `eval-lab/quant-sanity/llama70b-lc-ablation` in `ml-bench` cluster. Will update with artifact link.

Jonas Weber: Thanks all. Please treat as a P0 for gating (since this is exactly the kind of regression we don’t want to discover via customer reports).

Arjun Desai: :thumbsup: and once we have the ablation, we can decide: threshold-based gating vs "attention baseline" default for long-context. Either way, we should capture the rationale in the quant profile policy doc.
